invariant: A purchase of a course or community is priced by one of that entity's own (non-internal) payment plans; a planId belonging to another entity, or an internal plan, must be rejected.
summary: CourseLit allows Parameter Tampering via a payment plan associated with the wrong entity
notes: Fix commit referenced by the advisory (PR #574, 'Fixed a reported vulnerability'). POST /api/payment/initiate looked up the client-supplied planId in the whole domain (getPaymentPlan) without checking it belongs to entity.paymentPlans, so a cheaper or free plan of another entity could pay for this one; the fix adds that check and excludes internal plans (also in the webhook). Test, mock, jest config and package.json changes omitted. Classed limits (price chosen via a foreign plan); close to the frappe/lms batch case, which is classed workflow.

invariant: The price charged for a cart line is the Stripe price of the variant that the order records; the client must not choose the charged price (stripeId) independently of the delivered variant.
summary: External Control of Assumed-Immutable Web Parameter in the cart and checkout flow (price manipulation via client-supplied stripeId)
notes: Fix commit referenced by the advisory ('fix(security): derive Stripe price from the variant, not the client'). POST /api/user/cart stored a client-supplied stripeId (validated only as a non-empty string by minimalCartItemSchema in schema/cart.ts) next to variantId; POST /api/stripe/payment charged item.stripeId while the checkout.session.completed webhook recorded variantId. The fix resolves the price from the variant server-side (new src/lib/stripe/line-items.ts). Client files changed (AddToCart.tsx, useCartMutation.ts) are omitted. A small Next.js store template (about 250 stars). Classed limits (client-chosen price) though CWE-472.

invariant: The amount charged for a paid course, batch or certificate is the server-side price (minus server-validated discounts and plus tax); the client must not supply the amount, discount, tax or currency.
summary: Client-controlled price allows paid-course / certificate purchase for an arbitrary amount
notes: Advisory has no commit reference. Fix located in v2.52.0...v2.52.1: commit 1d04f4fd ('fix: allow zero amount checkout with coupons', PR #2292) removes the client-supplied amount, discount_amount, gst_amount, currency and redirect_to parameters of the whitelisted get_payment_link and recomputes them with get_order_summary on the server, matching the advisory's patch note. The same commit also changes frontend/src/pages/Billing.vue (client) and lms/lms/utils.py (refactor of update_payment_record into complete_enrollment); not listed.

invariant: An API token's allowed_rate_limit is set by the server; a user's PATCH of their own token must not raise it (the value is read-only / bounded server-side).
summary: Improper validation allows arbitrary modification of API token rate limits
notes: Fix commit edf24754 (#9148) cites GHSA-xfgr-2x3f-g2cf: allowed_rate_limit added to APITokenSerializer.Meta.read_only_fields (the changed hunk, old 22-27, class APITokenSerializer). The same commit also fixes GHSA-r5p8-cj3q-38cc (plaintext token logging) and refactors logging/cleanup tasks, all unrelated to this case. The views/api.py location (ApiTokenEndpoint.patch, PATCH /api/users/api-tokens/<pk>/ saving request.data through the serializer) is not a changed hunk; it is the request handler the fix protects. Also describable as mass assignment.

invariant: A shopping cart item's quantity must be at least 1, so a request cannot add a negative quantity that produces a negative line total and order total.
summary: Negative charge in shopping cart
notes: Fix is the merge of the GHSA private fork (merge commit; vulnerable_commit is its first parent). The fix clamps item.getQuantity() < 1 to 1 in addItemsToShoppingCart and addToCart(Customer, ...), and treats availability quantity <= 0 as unavailable in both createCartItem overloads. Two hunks of the fix (old 554-561 and 720-726) only remove @SuppressWarnings annotations and are omitted. The quantity arrives from the REST/controller cart endpoints that call this facade.

invariant: An order is priced and paid only in a currency the channel offers, and changing the order's currency re-prices its lines; a request-supplied currencyCode outside the channel's availableCurrencyCodes must be rejected.
summary: Insecure currencyCode handling allows wrong payment amounts
notes: Fix is two consecutive commits that cite the GHSA: fee503ff6f02 (reject a ?currencyCode= query value not in channel.availableCurrencyCodes in RequestContextService.getCurrencyCode) and f544cf375fbf (re-price order lines when the order currency changes, OrderService.applyPriceAdjustments). vulnerable_commit is the parent of fee503ff; fee503ff does not touch order.service.ts so its range holds. The attacker value is a query-string currency code, not a number; classed limits as an out-of-domain request value reaching the stored order (amount paid in a foreign currency with unconverted prices).

invariant: Initial setup creates exactly one super user (instance administrator): the 'no users yet' check and the user creation must be atomic so concurrent POST /api/v1/users/super requests cannot each create an administrator.
summary: Super User Creation Race Condition Allows Multiple Instance Administrators
notes: Fix commit cites the GHSA (#41681): signupAndLoginSuper checked userService.isUsersEmpty() and then created the user, non-atomically (Spring WebFlux + MongoDB); the fix first claims a one-time sentinel (claimSuperUserCreationSlot, atomic upsert added to CustomUserRepositoryCEImpl / UserServiceCEImpl, seeded by a new migration). The isUsersEmpty location (CustomUserRepositoryCEImpl old 35-44) is the check being raced, not a changed hunk (the fix inserts the new claim method after it at old 43-48). UserServiceCE/UserServiceCEImpl/CustomUserRepositoryCE only gain the new methods; omitted.

invariant: A promotion code with a usage limit is redeemed at most `limit` times: reading promotion.used, checking it against the limit and writing used+1 must be serialized across concurrent cart completions.
summary: Race condition in Medusa promotion registerUsage() allows bypassing promotion usage limits
notes: Unreviewed (NVD) advisory; references only PR #13760, which INTRODUCED the usage-limit feature (vulnerable code), not a fix. The researcher write-up pins registerUsage() lines 339-352, which match this parent exactly. No commit touched promotion-module.ts between Dec 2025 and 0b678b4c (Jul 2026, PR #16097, closes #16012), which locks the promotion rows that carry a numeric limit (and budget rows) FOR UPDATE and re-reads them before the guard. The fix is not explicitly tied to the CVE in its message; its tests cover budget and per-attribute races rather than promotion.limit, so a scorer should treat registerUsage as the target. The 339-352 location is the CVE-cited check, not a changed hunk. registerUsage runs on cart completion (store POST /store/carts/:id/complete).

invariant: Instance bootstrap creates exactly one instance admin: the 'no admin yet' check and the InstanceAdmin creation must be atomic (row lock on the Instance singleton) so concurrent sign-ups cannot both succeed.
summary: InstanceAdminSignUpEndpoint TOCTOU race allows two concurrent unauthenticated callers to both bootstrap as Plane instance admins
notes: Fix commit cites the GHSA (#9332). InstanceAdminSignUpEndpoint.post (POST /api/instances/admins/sign-up/) checks for an existing admin, then creates the user and InstanceAdmin without a lock; the fix wraps check and create in transaction.atomic() with select_for_update() on the Instance row. The fix's old 91-97 hunk is a small change at the start of the same post method and old 15-20 is imports; omitted.

invariant: An order can only claim stock that is still available: the StockQuantity check and its decrement in CreateOrder must happen atomically so concurrent checkouts cannot oversell or drive stock negative.
summary: Race condition in SimplCommerce CreateOrder allows bypassing inventory restrictions
notes: Unreviewed (NVD) advisory without a fix link. The fix is PR #1117 'Fix/#1111' (issue #1111 is titled 'Race Condition Vulnerability in CreateOrder Method (CVE-2024-53476)'), merged by fast-forward as five commits 9e52db0d..57c413c5; vulnerable_commit is the commit before the PR's first commit (compare 2c43b387...57c413c5 touches only OrderService.cs; the first parent of 57c413c5 is an intermediate PR commit). The check is at old line 221 (StockQuantity < Quantity) and the decrement at old line 259; the fix wraps the loop in a database transaction (default isolation), which a strict reviewer may not consider a complete fix. Reached from the checkout/payment controllers that call IOrderService.CreateOrder.

invariant: A public link with limitAccess N grants at most N accesses: checking nbAccess < limitAccess and incrementing nbAccess must be one conditional atomic update performed before the file or session is handed out.
summary: Non-atomic access counter allows concurrent requests to exceed public-link limits
notes: Advisory has no commit link; fix located in v2.5.0...v2.5.1: f1895c8d 'atomically enforce public link access limits'. checkLink reads nbAccess >= limitAccess, then linkAccess/linkDownload fire an unawaited unconditional nbAccess+1; the fix replaces it with consumeLinkAccess (UPDATE ... WHERE nbAccess < limitAccess, checked affected rows). Public link routes are under /api/app/link/*.

invariant: Stock can never be allocated beyond what is saleable: the saleable-stock check at checkout and the stockAllocated/stockOnHand updates must be atomic (row-locked or computed in SQL) so concurrent checkouts cannot oversell or lose updates.
summary: Stock Level Race Condition Allows Inventory Overselling via Concurrent Checkout
notes: Advisory has no commit link; fix is the 'Merge commit from fork' 92e4f356 (squash of the GHSA-8ghm-q833-cmgp branch) that last touched stock-level.service.ts before v3.7.4. The advisory text pins the vulnerable code at a5fd670f: updateStockAllocatedForLocation / updateStockOnHandForLocation read-modify-write, the ArrangingPayment guard in default-order-process.ts calling getSaleableStockLevel without a lock, and createAllocationsForOrderLines. The fix is large (also stock location strategies, order-modifier, new lock helpers); only the core read/check/write locations are listed. The ArrangingPayment transition is reached from the Shop API transitionOrderToState mutation.

invariant: An invitation is used at most maxUses times and a user never exceeds their file/URL quota: the limit check and the write that consumes it (invite.uses+1, file or URL creation) must be one atomic step.
summary: Race Condition (TOCTOU) in Invite Code Usage Limit, Storage Quota, and URL Quota Allows Bypass via Concurrent Requests
notes: Advisory has no commit link; the fix is the 'Merge commit from fork' 5c4a14c8 in v4.6.5...v4.7.0 (the only fork merge; touches exactly the invite, upload-quota and URL-quota paths named in the advisory). Anonymous Fastify route handlers have function null: register.ts is the POST /api/auth/register handler (invite read, check uses >= maxUses, then update uses: invite.uses + 1), upload/index.ts is POST /api/upload, upload/partial.ts the partial-upload handler, user/urls/index.ts is POST /api/user/urls (count then create). The primary business-logic sink is the invite usage limit in register.ts. src/offload/partial.ts (old 228-233, runComplete) is also touched by the fix and omitted (offload worker).

invariant: Content under an approval workflow is published only by a user with reviewer permission on the current state; completing the workflow must enforce the same HasStateReviewerPermission check as CompleteState and DiscardState.
summary: Content approval workflow bypass
notes: Advisory has no commit link. The fix is in 9cf39bcb ('Misc fixes', between v10.3.2 and v10.3.3, the patched version; it bundles fixes for several DNN advisories published together on 2026-08-25). GitHub shows WorkflowEngine.cs as a whole-file change because the commit converts it to a file-scoped namespace (re-indentation); an indentation-insensitive diff shows the only behavioural change is a new HasStateReviewerPermission guard in CompleteWorkflow (inserted after old line 303, with GetWorkflow moved up from old line 314). The line range is that method on the parent, not a GitHub hunk header. CompleteState (old 111) and DiscardState (old 172) already had the check.

invariant: Only an offer whose status is active can be redeemed at subscription checkout; archived offers must be rejected.
summary: Archived Offers can be Redeemed
notes: Advisory has no commit reference; fix located as the only offer-related commit between v6.54.0 and v6.54.1 (patched version). The fix inserts an offer.status !== 'active' check after the offer lookup in _getSubscriptionCheckoutData, reached from createCheckoutSession (POST /members/api/create-stripe-checkout-session).

invariant: A suspended (inactive) staff user cannot regain access: the self-service password reset must refuse to issue or redeem a reset token for an inactive user, as sign-in already does.
summary: Suspended Staff Could Reactivate Accounts with Password Reset
notes: Advisory has no commit reference; fix is the only password-reset/status commit between v6.61.0 and v6.62.0. The user status field is checked at sign-in but not in the reset flow; fix adds user.isInactive() checks in generateToken and doReset. The fix's hunks in ghost/core/core/server/models/user.js only change comments and the messages hunk of passwordreset.js only adds a string; both omitted. Advisory CWE is 862.

invariant: In the reset-credentials flow the password can be set only after the user followed the emailed verification link (action token for that user); switching authenticators via 'try another way' must not complete the email step.
summary: Keycloak: Unauthenticated account takeover via reset-credentials flow bypass
notes: Fix commit referenced by the advisory (closes CVE-2026-18963, PR #51844). ResetCredentialEmail.action() called context.success() unconditionally, so a POSTed action reaching it (via the 'tryAnotherWay' selector state kept as a boolean auth note) completed the email-verification step without the action token; the fix requires the action-token user id to match, and binds the selector note to the execution id. The AuthenticationProcessor.java hunk only edits a comment (omitted).

invariant: Enrollment in a paid course requires a payment for that course, or membership of a batch that actually contains that course; membership of an unrelated batch must not skip the payment check.
summary: Enrollment bypass in paid courses via unrelated batch
notes: Advisory has no commit reference. Fix found in v2.51.0...v2.52.0: c3e3337d 'fix(enrollment): prevent unauthorised enrollments in paid courses' (also cherry-picked as 1fb95b42). With enrollment_from_batch set to any batch the member belongs to, the validator returned early before the paid_course payment check; the fix requires a Batch Course row linking that batch to the course. The enrollment record is created by a client call (LMS Enrollment insert).

invariant: A user an administrator deactivated (is_active = false) cannot sign in, and signing in never flips is_active back to true.
summary: Disabled User Auto-Reactivation on Login
notes: Fix commit cites the GHSA (#9290). save_user_data set user.is_active = True on every login and complete_login_or_signup had no is_active guard; the fix adds the guard and removes the reactivation. The same commit also fixes WorkspaceOwnerPermission in app/permissions/workspace.py and utils/permissions/workspace.py (a separate issue; omitted), and its old 19-32 hunk of base.py only removes imports.

invariant: An organization invite (member id + token) admits exactly one account; the pending-invite state must be held server-side, not in a client-editable cookie that lets the same invite be applied to further accounts.
summary: Invite code reuse via cookie manipulation
notes: Advisory has no commit link; fix found as the only invite_helper.py change before 22.11.0 whose message states the cookie-manipulation reuse: 565f971d 'Move invite code functionality from cookie to session' (#40905). The pending-invite cookie (memberId, token) set by add_invite_cookie and read by get_invite_cookie / from_cookie_or_email / from_cookie is client-editable. invite_helper.py old 17-66 covers add_invite_cookie, remove_invite_cookie, get_invite_cookie and the start of from_cookie_or_email. The same commit renames the cookie helpers at call sites in src/sentry/auth/helper.py, src/sentry/web/frontend/auth_login.py and user_authenticator_enroll.py (mechanical renames, omitted). Classed workflow (invite not consumed per account).

invariant: Account recovery requires two DISTINCT valid recovery codes; one recovery code submitted twice (in any normalized form) must count once.
summary: Password recovery accepts one recovery code twice after whitespace normalization
notes: Fix commit named in the advisory's patched field ('Patch GHSA-vv8w-wg6r-hq56'). recoverAccount deduplicated raw inputs with a Set before trimming, so 'CODE' and ' CODE' both survived and each matched the same stored hash; the fix trims before deduplicating and consumes each matched hash once. Reached unauthenticated via the account-recovery endpoint (POST /system/recover-account in server/endpoints/system.js).

invariant: An execute-actions email action token is single-use: once the required actions it carries (e.g. WebAuthn registration) are completed, the same token must not be accepted again.
summary: Keycloak: Unauthorized account takeover via WebAuthn token replay
notes: Fix commit referenced by the advisory ('Make all required actions one time action by default', closes CVE-2026-37982, PR #49126). RequiredActionFactory.isOneTimeAction() defaulted to false, so required actions without an override (WebAuthn register) left ExecuteActionsActionToken reusable; the fix makes the default true. The fix also deletes now-redundant isOneTimeAction() overrides returning true in DeleteAccount, RecoveryAuthnCodesAction, UpdatePassword and UpdateTotp (no behaviour change; omitted). The token is consumed in the action-token handling for execute-actions (ExecuteActionsActionTokenHandler, services module), which consults isOneTimeAction.

invariant: A TOTP code that has been accepted once for a user's time step must be rejected on any further use (RFC 6238 5.2).
summary: TOTP tokens can be reused
notes: Advisory has no commit link; fix is the 'Merge commit from fork' d323fe00 ('Prevent the reuse of used TOTP tokens'), the only change to UserAuthService.ts before 2026.6.0. twoFactorAuthenticate validated the TOTP (window 5) without recording used steps; the fix stores 2fa:used:<user>:<step> in Redis with NX and narrows the window. The other hunk (old 4-20) only changes imports/constructor injection. Called from the sign-in and 2FA-protected API endpoints (SigninApiService and others).

invariant: An email (magic-link) sign-in token can be redeemed only once; a second redemption, including a concurrent one, must be refused.
summary: Email sign-in token has no server-side redemption check
notes: Fix commit is linked from the advisory (a5896210, PR #14089 'Tighten email sign-in link handling'). getUserForEmailSigninToken validates type, expiry, IP and signature but never records redemption; the fix claims the token hash in Redis with NX. Called from emailCallback in plugins/email/server/auth/email.ts (GET /auth/email.callback). Other hunks are doc comments (server/models/User.ts, jwt.ts old 106-117) and a new Redis key helper (RedisPrefixHelper.ts); omitted. The whole function body (old ~116-148) is the vulnerable code; the changed hunk is its return.

invariant: An MFA recovery code is single-use: a successful login with a recovery code must remove that code from the stored recovery list so the same code is rejected afterwards.
summary: MFA recovery codes not consumed after use
notes: Fix commit cites the GHSA (PR #10170, alpha branch). MFAAdapter.validateLogin accepted recovery[0] or recovery[1] and returned without updating the stored recovery list; the fix splices the used code out and saves it. Reached from POST /login with authData.mfa.token. The other hunk of mfa.js (old 39-44) is a doc comment and is omitted.

invariant: An account activation or password-recovery link works once: after it has been used to set the password it must be rejected for the rest of its validity period.
summary: Vulnerability-Lookup authentication weakness in account activation and password-recovery tokens (replayable)
notes: The global advisory's only commit reference (bef83724, 'gate SSE stream on active and confirmed account', AUTH-VULN-01) is a DIFFERENT fix from the same PR #552. The fix for this advisory is c97aa9d5 'make account activation/recovery tokens single-use (AUTH-VULN-02)' in that PR. The confirm_account view (GET/POST /confirm_account/<token>) validated a stateless URLSafeTimedSerializer token on signature and age only and never recorded use; the fix binds a nonce digest stored on the user and consumes it. user_utils.py old 1-32 covers generate_confirmation_token and confirm_token. website/models/user.py only gains new helper methods (issue/verify/consume_account_token); omitted.

invariant: Guesses of the current password on the authenticated password-change endpoint are throttled and locked out like login attempts, so a hijacked session cannot brute-force the password.
summary: No Attempt Throttling on Authenticated Password-Change Endpoint Enables Unlimited Current-Password Guessing
notes: Advisory has no commit link; the fix is part of f84fd41c 'Merge all draft security advisories (#5631)', the only change to settings/index.js before 4.33.0. That commit fixes many unrelated advisories in other files; only its settings/index.js hunks belong to this case (a comment-only hunk at old 35-41 omitted). handlePasswordProtectedSubform calls apos.user.verifyPassword with no attempt counter; the fix adds checkPasswordAttempts (login-module throttle, under a lock). Route: PATCH /api/v1/@apostrophecms/settings/password -> handleProtectedSubform -> handlePasswordChangeSubform -> handlePasswordProtectedSubform.

invariant: Failed web UI password checks are throttled, so the unauthenticated login and sign-in-token endpoints cannot be used to guess the password at full speed.
summary: Web UI login endpoints allow unlimited password guessing
notes: Advisory has no commit link; fix is PR #7339 'Add login throttle' (single commit 30b35f51, merged as 940edb5b), the brute-force fix before the 2.4.0.1 patched release. Endpoints are ASP.NET Core minimal-API lambdas registered in Auth.Map: POST /api/v1/auth/login (calls LoginProvider.PerformLoginWithPasswordAsync, the VerifyWebserverPassword check at old line 80) and POST /api/v1/auth/issuesignintoken (inline VerifyWebserverPassword, old line 113). The fix adds new files ILoginAttemptThrottle.cs / LoginAttemptThrottle.cs / TooManyRequestsException.cs and registers the throttle in Extensions/ServiceCollectionsExtensions.cs (old 62-67, DI wiring; omitted). LoginProvider.cs old 26-32 only adds the constructor parameter.

invariant: Brute-force protection allows at most the configured number of failed password guesses per user even when login attempts arrive in parallel; a login for a user must not proceed while another attempt for that user is still being evaluated.
summary: Keycloak Services has a potential bypass of brute force protection
notes: Fix commit d78b3072 is in the global advisory's references ('Support for blocking concurrent requests when brute force is enabled', closes #31726). The fix adds a NEW class DefaultBlockingBruteForceProtector (overrides isTemporarilyDisabled / isPermanentlyLockedOut to refuse a second in-flight attempt per user) and wires it in DefaultBruteForceProtectorFactory.postInit (changed hunk old 28-48). The DefaultBruteForceProtector locations are NOT changed hunks: they are the protected checks (failedLogin queues the failure asynchronously; the checks read state before the lock is recorded). Could also be classed race.

invariant: Every failed TOTP or recovery-code attempt counts toward the account lockout limit (USER_MAX_PASSWORD_ATTEMPTS), including attempts through the desktop sync client registration endpoint.
summary: TOTP Brute-Force via `POST /api/app/sync/register`
notes: Advisory has no commit link; fix located in v2.3.0...v2.4.0: b13a4aad 'increment failed attempts for 2FA-enabled users'. On a failed attempt by a TOTP-enabled user, updateAccesses chose 'preserve' instead of 'increment', so the counter never reached the lockout limit. The attacker-reachable caller is SyncClientsManager.register (backend/src/applications/sync/services/sync-clients-manager.service.ts, updateAccesses(user, ip, false) after a rejected TOTP and recovery code; route POST /api/app/sync/register marked @AuthTokenSkip in sync.controller.ts). The preceding commit 285b8707 ('update failed login attempts atomically') is the vulnerable_commit and still has the bug.

invariant: Second-factor (TOTP/WebAuthn/recovery code) verification attempts are rate limited per session like password sign-in, so an attacker with the password cannot guess OTP codes without limit.
summary: Lack of rate limiting when verifying second factor
notes: Fix is PR #14918 linked from the advisory (merge f8062934); main commit 76a7e50d adds @method_decorator(session_ratelimit_post('second_factor')) to SecondFactorLoginView.dispatch (OTP form POST, verification in form_valid) and to the WebAuthn WeblateCompleteCredentialAuthenticationView. Other files in the PR are docs.

invariant: Repeated failed logins for an account or client are locked out (after 5 failures for 30 minutes in the fix), so passwords cannot be guessed without limit.
summary: wger vulnerable to brute force attempts
notes: Advisory references 5e3167e3, the head of PR #1143 'Configuring django axes' (message 'Merge branch master into add-django-axes'); its FIRST parent is the feature branch, so vulnerable_commit is the PR base / master tip f38a27c6 (the second parent), and ranges are on f38a27c6 (compare f38a27c6...5e3167e3). The fix is configuration only: django-axes added to INSTALLED_APPS, MIDDLEWARE and AUTHENTICATION_BACKENDS plus AXES_* settings (settings_global.py). The protected handler is the login route (core/urls.py: views.LoginView.as_view with UserLoginForm; views/user.py login). The registration hunk only passes request= to authenticate() (needed by axes). Formatting-only hunks of settings_global.py omitted.
